```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 7, dpi = 96
)
# sdvplotR's team-colored courts need sportyR 2.4.5 or later
has_surface <- requireNamespace("sdvplotR", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("sportyR", quietly = TRUE) &&
  utils::packageVersion("sportyR") >= "2.4.5"
```

**A shot chart puts every field-goal attempt where it happened.** It is the most direct picture of how a player or team scores, and with `hoopR`'s shot loaders and a court drawn by [sportyR](https://sportyR.sportsdataverse.org/) it takes a few lines of `ggplot2`. This article covers make/miss charts, hexbin and density maps, shot zones and field-goal percentage (FG%) by zone, for the NBA and men's college basketball. Every chart is computed from one season of release data, filtered to one player where possible to keep it fast.

New to `hoopR`? Read [Getting Started with hoopR](getting-started-hoopR.html) first.

## Packages

```{r packages}
library(hoopR)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sportyR)   # install.packages("sportyR")

season <- 2026     # the 2025-26 season
```

[sdvplotR](https://sdvplotR.sportsdataverse.org/) is optional. It adds `sdv_court_coords()`, which converts NBA Stats shot locations to sportyR's court frame, and `sdv_surface()`, which paints a sportyR court in a team's colors:

```{r install_sdvplotr, eval = FALSE}
pak::pak("sportsdataverse/sdvplotR")
```

## Which shot data does hoopR have, and in which coordinate frame?

Shot locations come in different frames, and mixing them up is the most common shot-chart bug.

| Loader | Source | Location columns | Frame |
|---|---|---|---|
| `load_nba_shots()` | ESPN NBA play-by-play | `coordinate_x`, `coordinate_y` | Feet from center court; each team's shots at the basket it attacks. Plot directly. |
| `load_mbb_shots()` | ESPN men's college play-by-play | `coordinate_x`, `coordinate_y` | Same as above. A few rows hold placeholder values far off the court. |
| `load_nba_stats_shots()` | NBA Stats API | `x_legacy`, `y_legacy` | Tenths of a foot, origin at the hoop. Convert with `sdvplotR::sdv_court_coords()`. |
| `load_ncaa_mbb_shots()` | stats.ncaa.org engine | see its reference page | NCAA shot events from the play-by-play engine. |

sportyR draws courts with the origin at center court, in feet: `x` runs along the court from -47 to 47 and `y` across it from -25 to 25. The left basket is at `x = -41.75`. `geom_basketball("nba", display_range = "defense")` draws the left half.

## A make/miss chart for an NBA player

`load_nba_shots()` holds every shot ESPN charted. We drop free throws, pick the player with the most field-goal attempts, and turn shots at the right-hand basket half a turn (flip both signs) so every shot lands at the left basket.

```{r nba_shots}
nba_shots <- load_nba_shots(seasons = season) |>
  filter(!grepl("Free Throw", type_text))

volume <- nba_shots |>
  count(athlete_id_1, athlete_name_1, team_abbrev, name = "fga", sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 1)
volume

player_shots <- nba_shots |>
  filter(athlete_id_1 == volume$athlete_id_1) |>
  mutate(
    right = coordinate_x > 0,
    x = if_else(right, -coordinate_x, coordinate_x),
    y = if_else(right, -coordinate_y, coordinate_y),
    result = if_else(scoring_play, "Made", "Missed")
  )
```

```{r nba_make_miss, fig.alt = "Half-court NBA shot chart of the 2025-26 league leader in field-goal attempts, with made shots as filled circles and misses as crosses."}
geom_basketball("nba", display_range = "defense") +
  geom_point(aes(x, y), data = filter(player_shots, result == "Missed"),
             shape = 4, colour = "grey30", size = 1.3, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(x, y), data = filter(player_shots, result == "Made"),
             shape = 21, fill = "#2C3D50", colour = "white", stroke = 0.2, size = 1.8) +
  labs(
    title = paste0(volume$athlete_name_1, ": every field-goal attempt, 2025-26"),
    subtitle = sprintf("%d made (filled), %d missed (crosses), %.1f%% FG",
                       sum(player_shots$scoring_play), sum(!player_shots$scoring_play),
                       100 * mean(player_shots$scoring_play)),
    caption = "Data: hoopR::load_nba_shots() (ESPN). Court: sportyR"
  )
```

### The same chart on a team-colored court

`sdvplotR::sdv_surface()` wraps `geom_basketball()` and paints the lane and apron in a team's colors. It needs sportyR 2.4.5 or later.

```{r nba_surface, eval = has_surface, fig.alt = "The same half-court shot chart drawn on a court painted in the player's team colors."}
library(sdvplotR)

sdv_surface("nba", volume$team_abbrev, display_range = "defense") +
  geom_point(aes(x, y, fill = result), data = player_shots,
             shape = 21, colour = "grey15", stroke = 0.2, size = 1.7, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Made = "white", Missed = "grey35"), name = NULL) +
  labs(title = paste0(volume$athlete_name_1, ", 2025-26"),
       caption = "Data: hoopR::load_nba_shots(). Court: sdvplotR + sportyR") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Where do shots come from? Hexbin maps

With hundreds of overlapping points a scatter plot saturates. A **hexbin** map counts attempts in small hexagons instead. Here is the whole league, which needs the `hexbin` package:

```{r league_hex, fig.alt = "Hexbin map of every NBA field-goal attempt in 2025-26 on a half court, colored by the log count of attempts, showing clusters at the rim and beyond the three-point line."}
league_shots <- nba_shots |>
  mutate(
    right = coordinate_x > 0,
    x = if_else(right, -coordinate_x, coordinate_x),
    y = if_else(right, -coordinate_y, coordinate_y)
  ) |>
  filter(x <= 0)

geom_basketball("nba", display_range = "defense") +
  geom_hex(aes(x, y), data = league_shots, binwidth = c(1.5, 1.5), alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", name = "Attempts") +
  labs(title = "Where NBA shots came from, 2025-26",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s field-goal attempts", format(nrow(league_shots), big.mark = ",")),
       caption = "Data: hoopR::load_nba_shots()")
```

The two clusters, at the rim and just beyond the three-point line, are the modern shot profile: the mid-range is comparatively empty. Coloring each hexagon by its make rate instead of its count shows *efficiency* by location (`stat_summary_hex()` averages `z` in each bin):

```{r league_hex_fg, fig.alt = "Hexbin map of NBA field-goal percentage by court location in 2025-26, limited to hexagons with at least 30 attempts."}
geom_basketball("nba", display_range = "defense") +
  stat_summary_hex(
    aes(x, y, z = as.numeric(scoring_play)), data = league_shots,
    fun = \(z) if (length(z) >= 30) mean(z) else NA_real_,
    binwidth = c(2, 2), alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdBu", direction = 1, limits = c(0.2, 0.8),
                       oob = scales::squish, name = "FG%", na.value = NA) +
  labs(title = "NBA field-goal percentage by location, 2025-26",
       subtitle = "Hexagons with at least 30 attempts",
       caption = "Data: hoopR::load_nba_shots()")
```

## Smooth density maps

A two-dimensional kernel density estimate smooths the same information into contours, which reads well for a single player:

```{r player_density, fig.alt = "Filled density contours of the selected NBA player's shot locations on a half court."}
geom_basketball("nba", display_range = "defense") +
  stat_density_2d_filled(aes(x, y), data = player_shots, alpha = 0.7,
                         contour_var = "ndensity", bins = 8) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues", guide = "none") +
  labs(title = paste0(volume$athlete_name_1, ": shot density, 2025-26"),
       caption = "Data: hoopR::load_nba_shots()")
```

## Shot zones and FG% by zone

Zones turn a chart into a table. A standard five-zone split:

- **Restricted area**: within 4 feet of the basket.
- **Paint (non-restricted area)**: the rest of the lane (16 feet wide in the NBA, 12 in college, 19 feet deep from the baseline).
- **Mid-range**: every other two-point attempt.
- **Corner 3**: three-pointers from the straight part of the line along the sideline.
- **Above-the-break 3**: every other three.

Zone boundaries need to know whether an attempt was a three. ESPN's NBA shot file records `score_value = 0` for misses, so it cannot tell a missed three from a missed two. The NBA Stats file can: `shot_value` is the attempt's value. We use `load_nba_stats_shots()` (note it takes the season's **start** year) and convert its legacy coordinates with `sdv_court_coords()`, which divides by ten and moves the origin to center court so the shots fit `geom_basketball()`.

```{r zone_fn}
# Approximate zone geometry on sportyR's frame (basket at x = -41.75, feet).
shot_zone <- function(x, y, is_three, paint_half_width = 8, corner_depth = 14) {
  dist <- sqrt((x + 41.75)^2 + y^2)
  case_when(
    is_three & x <= -47 + corner_depth & abs(y) >= 20 ~ "Corner 3",
    is_three ~ "Above-the-break 3",
    dist <= 4 ~ "Restricted area",
    abs(y) <= paint_half_width & x <= -47 + 19 ~ "Paint (non-RA)",
    TRUE ~ "Mid-range"
  )
}
zone_levels <- c("Restricted area", "Paint (non-RA)", "Mid-range", "Corner 3", "Above-the-break 3")
```

```{r nba_stats_shots, eval = requireNamespace("sdvplotR", quietly = TRUE)}
stats_shots <- load_nba_stats_shots(seasons = season - 1) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  sdvplotR::sdv_court_coords(x_column = "x_legacy", y_column = "y_legacy") |>
  filter(season_type_id == 2) |>                      # regular season
  mutate(
    made = shot_result == "Made",
    zone = factor(shot_zone(court_x, court_y, shot_value == 3), levels = zone_levels)
  )

league_zones <- stats_shots |>
  group_by(zone) |>
  summarise(fga = n(), fg_pct = mean(made), pts_per_shot = mean(made * shot_value)) |>
  mutate(share = fga / sum(fga))

league_zones |>
  mutate(across(c(fg_pct, pts_per_shot, share), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

**Points per shot** (FG% times the shot's value) is the fair comparison across zones: a three only needs to go in two-thirds as often as a two to be worth the same.

Now one player against the league. We take the NBA Stats leader in field-goal attempts (its `player_name` is a short name):

```{r player_zones, eval = requireNamespace("sdvplotR", quietly = TRUE)}
target <- stats_shots |>
  count(person_id, player_name, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 1)
target

player_zones <- stats_shots |>
  filter(person_id == target$person_id) |>
  group_by(zone) |>
  summarise(fga = n(), fg_pct = mean(made)) |>
  left_join(select(league_zones, zone, league_fg_pct = fg_pct), by = "zone") |>
  mutate(diff = fg_pct - league_fg_pct)

player_zones |>
  mutate(across(c(fg_pct, league_fg_pct, diff), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

```{r zone_plot, eval = requireNamespace("sdvplotR", quietly = TRUE), fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Bar chart comparing the selected player's field-goal percentage with the NBA league average in each of five shot zones."}
player_zones |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(fg_pct, league_fg_pct), names_to = "who", values_to = "pct") |>
  mutate(who = if_else(who == "fg_pct", target$player_name, "League")) |>
  ggplot(aes(zone, pct, fill = who)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2C3D50", "#A7C6E6"), name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "FG% by shot zone vs league average, 2025-26 regular season",
       x = NULL, y = "FG%", caption = "Data: hoopR::load_nba_stats_shots()") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

And the zones drawn on the court, to check the geometry:

```{r zone_map, eval = requireNamespace("sdvplotR", quietly = TRUE), fig.alt = "Half-court map of the selected player's shots colored by the five shot zones."}
geom_basketball("nba", display_range = "defense") +
  geom_point(aes(court_x, court_y, colour = zone),
             data = filter(stats_shots, person_id == target$person_id),
             size = 1.2, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set2", name = NULL) +
  labs(title = paste0(target$player_name, ": shots by zone, 2025-26"),
       caption = "Data: hoopR::load_nba_stats_shots(); coordinates via sdvplotR::sdv_court_coords()") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## A men's college basketball shot chart

`load_mbb_shots()` uses the same ESPN frame as the NBA file, and the college court has the same 94-foot floor and basket position, so the code barely changes. Two differences: the college file has a few placeholder coordinates far off the court, which we drop, and its `score_value` is the attempt's value (2 or 3) even for misses, so zones work directly.

```{r mbb_shots}
mbb_shots <- load_mbb_shots(seasons = season) |>
  filter(!grepl("FreeThrow", type_text),
         abs(coordinate_x) <= 47, abs(coordinate_y) <= 25) |>
  mutate(
    right = coordinate_x > 0,
    x = if_else(right, -coordinate_x, coordinate_x),
    y = if_else(right, -coordinate_y, coordinate_y),
    made = scoring_play,
    # college paint is 12 ft wide; the straight part of the arc is about 10 ft deep
    zone = factor(shot_zone(x, y, score_value == 3, paint_half_width = 6, corner_depth = 10),
                  levels = zone_levels)
  )

mbb_volume <- mbb_shots |>
  count(athlete_id_1, athlete_name_1, team_abbrev, name = "fga", sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 1)
mbb_volume
```

```{r mbb_chart, fig.alt = "Half-court college basketball shot chart for the 2025-26 Division I leader in field-goal attempts, with makes and misses distinguished."}
mbb_player <- filter(mbb_shots, athlete_id_1 == mbb_volume$athlete_id_1)

geom_basketball("ncaa", display_range = "defense") +
  geom_point(aes(x, y, shape = made, colour = made), data = mbb_player,
             size = 1.8, alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 4), labels = c("Missed", "Made"), name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#2C3D50", `FALSE` = "grey45"), labels = c("Missed", "Made"), name = NULL) +
  labs(title = paste0(mbb_volume$athlete_name_1, " (", mbb_volume$team_abbrev, "), 2025-26"),
       subtitle = sprintf("%d field-goal attempts, %.1f%% FG", nrow(mbb_player), 100 * mean(mbb_player$made)),
       caption = "Data: hoopR::load_mbb_shots() (ESPN). Court: sportyR") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

How does the college shot profile compare with the NBA's?

```{r compare_profiles, eval = requireNamespace("sdvplotR", quietly = TRUE)}
mbb_zones <- mbb_shots |>
  group_by(zone) |>
  summarise(fga = n(), fg_pct = mean(made)) |>
  mutate(share = fga / sum(fga))

bind_rows(
  mutate(league_zones, league = "NBA"),
  mutate(mbb_zones, league = "Men's college")
) |>
  select(league, zone, share, fg_pct) |>
  mutate(across(c(share, fg_pct), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = league, values_from = c(share, fg_pct))
```

## Caveats

- **Coordinates are charted by people.** ESPN and NBA Stats locations are recorded in-arena or from video and can be off by a foot or two; heaves and tip-ins near the rim are noisy.
- **Zone boundaries here are approximate.** The geometry above uses round numbers; the official three-point line has a slightly different corner depth, and shots on a line can land in either zone. Use the NBA Stats `shot_value` (or college `score_value`) for whether a shot was a three, never distance alone.
- **Small samples.** FG% in a zone with a few dozen attempts is noisy. Filter hexagons and zones by attempt counts, as above.
- **Frames.** Never pass ESPN `coordinate_x` / `coordinate_y` to `sdv_court_coords()`; it is for the NBA Stats legacy frame (and EuroLeague's, with `provider = "euroleague"`).
